contexts.text: They desire to destroy the soul also.
They are kept in the desire of revenge...
They are kept in the strongest desire of ascending into Heaven... Their desire is increased, and is more and more turned into anxiety...
From innate desire they regard all things with longing.
When the desire of breaking out thence is kindled...
From the predominant desire of innovating...
Originates from the desire which is of the external man.
Appetite and taste correspond to the desire for knowledges.
Diabolical Spirits desire nothing more than...
The delight, pleasure, and desire there, belong to the will, and are called natural goods.
They constantly had the desire and longing to come into Heaven. Such are they who relate to the ventricles of the brain... This endeavour (of the lymph) corresponds to this desire and longing.
They frequented places of worship, not from any longing to know the things of Heaven, but from another desire drawn from the time of early childhood.
The evil want to be eminent, to be enriched, and therefore to seem upright and zealous, and from this desire, as from a fire, are excited to do such things more than the upright.
As the man who is in this state desires nothing but evils... lest he should act as he desires... he is kept in bonds...
The desire always remaining.
The fire which burns before Him = the desire of evil; the flame which burns after Him = the desire of falsity thence.
They are kindled with a cruel desire of injuring.
Such a desire is innate to Spirits.
They desired the communication (of heavenly joy) to themselves, which was done; for what a Spirit who is not yet in Heaven or Hell desires, is granted to him, if it is advantageous...
For will they have desire. CL 291.
There are many things of love, to which other names have been allotted, because they are derivations; as affections, desires, appetites, and their pleasures and delights.
Natural affection, which in itself is desire... is what alone leads and moves beasts...
This desire lies inmostly concealed in hereditary evil...
Except some desire connected with the body.
They are in the lust of the adultery of a son with his mother.
As it verges towards the desire of varieties, and to the desire of defloration.
The desire seized me...
They still inwardly desired honour in the world... which desire it was granted me to perceive... That which is heavenly desires nothing of the kind...
Spirits desire, and induce their cupidity on man. Example(s).
There is still resistance from his desire of glory in life, which was such as almost to surpass the desires of all others.
That Spirits... perceive what man desires.

They had no affection for truth, justice and right, except from their own proper desire, which desire not only excited them, but also enlightened them; for such can enlighten their cupidity in civil things...
They desire to die () = that they want to destroy the faculty of perceiving good.
From him that would borrow of thee ().
They inspire into them the desire of going out...
